title: Precision gremlins: tracebook for INT8/FP8/BF16 NaN incidents
content:
TL;DR: ongoing, intermittent NaNs when serving certain long-context prompts with INT8 / FP8 mixed-mode runtime. Failure appears when sequence length > 2048 and when KV cache reuse + aggressive batching is enabled. This document is a personal tracebook of commands tried, logs captured, hypotheses, and quick repros.

1) Incident summary / how I first saw it
- Symptom: generation stalls then returns truncated tokens followed by 'nan' tokens and runtime exception in kernel. Sometimes model returns correct tokens then a sudden NaN token mid-sequence.
- First observed: 2026-02-14 in canary dedicated pool after a rollout of quantized model variant (int8 + bf16 residuals).
- Affected model variant: rwdx-13b-quant-int8-fp8-hybrid:v3 (new quant pipeline).
- Conditions: long prompts (2k+ tokens), KV cache enabled, batching enabled (batch_size >= 8), rotary embeddings on.

2) Environment snapshot (captured from canary node)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS
- CUDA: 12.1
- cuBLAS/cuDNN: cuBLAS 12.1 / cuDNN 9.8
- GPU: A100-PCIE-40GB, CUDA compute capability 8.0
- Driver: 535.86.05
- Python: 3.11.6
- PyTorch: 2.2.0 (custom build with --use-nnpack disabled, built on 2026-01-25)
- Serving runtime: serving-runtime v1.21.3-quant (PR #1447 applied locally)

3) Repro commands (start here to reproduce locally)
- Baseline single-request (no batching, fresh cache):
  export RUNTIME_FLAGS="KV_CACHE=1 BATCHING=0 QUANT_MODE=int8"
  python examples/infer_cli.py --model rwdx-13b-quant-int8-fp8-hybrid:v3 --prompt-file long_prompt_2200t.txt --max-tokens 512
- Fails intermittently; to increase repro rate, enable batching and repeated requests:
  export RUNTIME_FLAGS="KV_CACHE=1 BATCHING=1 BATCH_SIZE=8 QUANT_MODE=int8"
  ./scripts/stress_infer.sh --concurrency 16 --sequence-length 2500 --duration 10m --model rwdx-13b-quant-int8-fp8-hybrid:v3
- Quick single-command to reproduce NaN observed here on canary: (captured exact env)\  CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_KEEP_BLOAT=0 python -u examples/infer_stream.py --model rwdx-13b-quant-int8-fp8-hybrid:v3 --prompt "<long prompt omitted>" --max-toks 800 --use-kv-cache --batch-size 8

4) Representative error snippets (copied raw)
- Kernel error (from worker logs):
  E 2026-02-15 03:12:08.472 serving-runtime: kernel failed: warp-atan2-fused.cu: line 224: device-side assert: tenso r_norm is NaN
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/serving/runtime/infer_loop.py", line 412, in _generate
      out = self.model.forward_chunk(inputs)
    File "/opt/serving/runtime/model_wrapper.py", line 723, in forward_chunk
      kv = self.kv_cache.read(ctx_id)
    File "/opt/serving/runtime/kv_cache.py", line 210, in read
      assert not torch.isnan(kv_block).any(), "KV cache contains NaN"
  AssertionError: KV cache contains NaN

- Model output (example):
  ... "and then we observed", 0.134, 0.298, nan, nan, nan

5) Quick triage checklist tried (notes inline)
- Reproduce with FP32-only build: passes. => suggests quant path implicated.
- Disable KV cache: no NaNs. => cache reuse likely trigger.
- Reduce batch size to 1: failure rate drops but not eliminated for very long sequences.
- Force BF16 attention / residuals: mixed results; sometimes removes NaNs, sometimes not.
- Toggle stochastic rounding for FP8 quant: decreased failures when enabled (but not deterministic).
- Set environment FTZ (flush-to-zero) and DAZ off/on: flickering results; driver/ABI differences suspected.
- Run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1: makes failures deterministic and easier to capture stack.
- Run with torch.autocast disabled: failure rate drops (points at autocast interactions).

6) Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: KV cache memory layout / packing bug for quantized tensors (int8 compression + offset) causing stale/garbage values to be re-used for keys/values beyond certain offsets -> NaNs when fed into fused kernels.
- H2: FP8 stochastic rounding path + autocast interaction occasionally generates denormal values that later underflow/overflow in fused attention kernel leading to NaN.
- H3: Kernel-specific race condition when batching triggers a different kernel path (multi-stream copy + async quant-dequant) and an uninitialized workspace leads to NaN.
- H4: Rotary embedding scaling with mixed precision leads to large exponents in some positions (very long sequence) causing fp8 saturation then NaN in subsequent matmuls.

7) Experiments run (with short notes on outcome)
- E1: Zero-wipe KV cache before every read (inserts explicit torch.zeros_like on load): reduced incidence to near-zero in stress runs -> supports H1. Downside: huge perf regression.
- E2: Switch quant backend (quantize->fp32 dequant path) to use alternative rounding kernel (PR #1447): inconsistent improvement (~30% fewer failures).
- E3: Force denormals-handling on (via setenv CUDA_DISABLE_DENORM=0): no clear improvement.
- E4: Disable fused attention (fall back to slower but simpler kernel): no NaNs observed in 1M tokens test -> supports kernel bug / fusion path.
- E5: Run with KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 and single CPU thread to avoid host-side race: no effect.
- E6: Short-circuit rotary scaling > clip to 1e3: occasional suppression of NaN but not consistent.

8) Minimal repro snippet (python) — small script to provoke NaN reliably on canary
- Note: this is intentionally noisy; use with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and QUANT_MODE=int8.
  from time import sleep
  import torch
  from serving_runtime import ModelWrapper

  m = ModelWrapper.load('rwdx-13b-quant-int8-fp8-hybrid:v3')
  prompt = open('long_prompt_2500t.txt').read()
  toks = m.tokenize(prompt)
  # feed in chunks to populate KV cache and force mem fragmentation
  for i in range(0, len(toks), 128):
      chunk = toks[i:i+128]
      out = m.generate(chunk, max_new_tokens=64, batch_size=8, use_kv_cache=True)
      if 'nan' in str(out):
          print('NaN seen after chunk', i)
          break

9) Notes on instrumentation added
- Inserted KV cache checksum (simple XOR hash) and per-block sequence ids; found occasional mismatched seq_id on read -> suggests race or stale pointer.
- Added per-kernel inputs dump for fused-attn (first 1 found) and reproduced one instance in /tmp/quant-dumps/2026-02-16_0348.tar.gz (attached to JIRA-ENGINF-7382).

10) Observed patterns / edge signals
- Failures concentrate on tokens at positions ~2048-2600 (for our model's rotary window).
- Failures more frequent with multi-request batch mixing different context lengths (mixing cold and warmed contexts).
- When using bf16 for residuals + int8 for weights, NaNs occasional but less than pure int8 path.

11) Potential quick mitigations (to deploy to canary)
- Roll back quant variant for longest-running tenants (safe, immediate).
- Disable fused attention for quant models in canary (costly but stops failures).
- Add aggressive KV cache validation (checksum + drop and re-init on mismatch) for customer sessions hitting >2k tokens.

12) Longer-term fixes to investigate
- Audit KV cache packing/unpacking code paths for off-by-one offsets when sequence lengths > block_size (esp. in quantized plane).
- Harden fused attention kernels to check for NaNs in intermediate workspace and fallback to safe kernel if detected.
- Revisit PR #1447 quant rounding kernel and add unit tests with long-sequence simulation and randomized fill patterns.
- Add continuous fuzz test that runs mixed batch sizes, cold/warm contexts, stochastic rounding on/off across many iterations.

13) Next steps (my TODOs)
- [ ] Pair with Johan to trace the seq_id mismatch (we have kv-cache diffs saved) – target 2026-03-12
- [ ] Add unit test that simulates sequence wrap-around for KV pack/unpack – target 2026-03-15
- [ ] Add early-detect NaN sanitizer in fused-attn: if detected, dump kernel inputs and revert to safe path – target 2026-03-20
- [ ] Prepare short rollback playbook for SRE (steps + commands) to disable quant variant quickly — draft by 2026-03-13

14) Random notes / things to try later
- Try toggling MXCSR FTZ/DAZ bits via low-level instruction (linux-specific) to see effect on denorm handling.
- Run with ASAN-like instrumented CUDA runtime (if available) to detect out-of-bounds writes in kernels.
- Check allocator behaviour: fragmentation in GPU memory could cause pointer aliasing in our custom packer. Try running with MALLOC_TRIM and restricted GPU memory to reproduce.

Appendix: raw commands I used often
- stress_infer.sh (simple wrapper)
  #! /bin/bash
  for i in $(seq 1 $1); do
    python -u examples/infer_stream.py --model "$2" --prompt-file "$3" --max-toks $4 --use-kv-cache --batch-size $5 &
    sleep 0.2
  done
  wait

- capture logs with timestamps
  sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -o short-iso --since "2026-02-14" > /tmp/serving-runtime-trace-2026-02-14.log

Final: keep this doc messy — it is a personal tracebook. If you find new leads, append here (timestamp + short blurb).

Footnote: if you grab dumps, please upload to the JIRA ticket above and add notes about kernel abi versions.

-- Aisha
